If sentiment is consistently positive in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over the last 5 days, adjust forecast downward for mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect momentum reversal.

If sentiment is mixed or volatile in the last 5 days, apply a 1–2% downward bias to late-horizon (16–30 days) forecasts to hedge against uncertainty.

If sentiment is uniformly positive and price is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for late-horizon to prevent over-leverage on momentum.

If sentiment is uniformly negative and price is trending downward, increase forecast slope by 10–20% for late-horizon to reinforce bearish momentum.
